Scan to manage this TV from your phone, or open %1$s on a computer.
Token: %2$s

For the API, send it as: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Anything using the old token (Home Assistant, scripts) stops working until you update it.
This TV has no screen for that permission. From a computer, run:\n\nadb shell appops set %1$s SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow
Saved to %1$s (without secrets).\n\nCopy it with: adb pull %1$s
No file at %1$s.\n\nCopy one there with: adb push settings.json %1$s
Choose what this TV shows: a Home Assistant dashboard or any web page.
This TV\'s web engine isn\'t working

The app shows pages with Android System WebView. It\'s missing, turned off or being updated. Update or turn on Android System WebView (or Chrome) in the TV\'s app store or Settings → Apps, then try again.
Showing the dashboard as it was at %1$s. Trying again by itself in %2$d seconds.
This TV needs to sign in to Home Assistant once. If Home Assistant trusts this TV it takes one click; otherwise use the TV user\'s username and password.
Home Assistant no longer accepts this TV\'s sign-in. Sign in again.
Tip: typing is easier with the Google TV app on your phone, or a USB keyboard.
The login page took too long to load. Check that Home Assistant is running and the address in settings is right.
Home Assistant sent back an unexpected answer. Try again.
This TV is signed in to Home Assistant at %1$s.
Enter the dashboard\'s start URL in settings first, then sign in.
Sign in once on this TV instead
This TV forgets its sign-in and shows the sign-in screen until you sign in again.
Set to use a long-lived access token, but none is saved
The Home Assistant page handles sign-in (its own login page or trusted_networks)
Let the Home Assistant page handle sign-in
Paste a long-lived access token from the TV user\'s Home Assistant profile (Security tab). Typing is easier from the Google TV app on your phone.
↑ ↓ choose · → open · ← back\nChanges save straight away
Off: stay on the start page
Pick from your Home Assistant dashboards and panels
The page this TV opens. Easier: use Choose a dashboard.
Only needed if the start page isn\'t on Home Assistant itself. Leave empty to use the start page\'s address.
Enter your Home Assistant address, for example http://192.168.1.50:8123
Shows only the dashboard, without Home Assistant\'s own menus
Opens Home Assistant\'s login page. If Home Assistant trusts this TV, it\'s one click.
Paste a token from the TV user\'s profile instead of signing in
Show Home Assistant\'s own login page inside the dashboard
Stops the TV\'s screensaver while the dashboard shows
Opens the dashboard when the TV turns on
Jump between buttons (recommended): arrows move between clickable items, OK presses
On-screen pointer: arrows move a pointer, OK taps under it
Let the page handle the arrows
Hold OK or press Menu for the quick menu: reload, pointer, start page, settings. Back goes to the TV home screen.
Reload if Home Assistant is unreachable for
Failed loads are retried, and a crashed or frozen page is replaced, automatically.
Allowed: pop-ups show over Netflix, YouTube and everything else
Not allowed yet, so pop-ups only show on the dashboard. Press OK to fix.
A sample like a doorbell pop-up, with your settings below
Lets Home Assistant control this TV over your network, with a token
Anything using the old token stops working
For automations written for TvOverlay. No token: anything on your network can show pop-ups.
Adds this TV to Home Assistant through MQTT discovery
The broker\'s address, usually Home Assistant\'s IP
The full address, starting with https:// or http://.
Pages take turns; using the remote holds the current one
Rotate through several pages, e.g. a dashboard and a calendar
For tablets and wall displays: press Home and choose OpenPane, "Always". Turn off to go back to the usual home screen.
Once a day, asks GitHub whether a newer release is out. Never installs anything by itself.
OpenPane %1$s is out: get it from github.com/mattgrechtech/openpane/releases
Colour keys and digits to Home Assistant
While the dashboard is in front, the red, green, yellow and blue keys and 0-9 send a openpane_key event (short or long press) for your automations.
Moves the page a few pixels every couple of minutes. For OLED screens that show the dashboard all day.
For example a Home Assistant dashboard with a photo frame or a big clock and weather. The dashboard comes back when someone is around.
Off: at night only a button press wakes the screen.
Yes: this TV lets the app turn the screen on and come to the front.
Can\'t come to the front: allow \"display over other apps\" (see Pop-ups).
Can\'t turn the screen on: run tools/provision again, or adb shell appops set %s TURN_SCREEN_ON allow.
In standby this TV cuts apps off the network: Home Assistant must switch the TV on first (see the wake-on-motion guide).
Home Assistant tells the TV when your motion or presence sensors see someone. Resting keeps the page running behind a dark screen, so it\'s back at once. Any button also wakes it.
The dashboard goes black but keeps running, so pop-ups still show. Any button wakes it for 5 minutes. To switch the TV itself off, use your TV\'s own sleep timer or Home Assistant.
Choose Home Assistant or a web page, find the server and sign in
Pop-ups with buttons can take the remote
Over other apps too: OK presses a button, Back closes the pop-up. While one is up, the remote doesn\'t control the app behind it.
On the dashboard, Back closes the newest pop-up. Home Assistant can close one with notify/clear and its id. Each pop-up can set its own size, corner and time.
What should this TV show? You can change this later in Settings.
Scan a code, then sign in to Home Assistant on your phone. No typing with the remote.
Scan with your phone\'s camera (same Wi-Fi as the TV), then use Sign in to Home Assistant. Or open %1$s.
A dashboard from your Home Assistant, with pop-ups and control from automations
Any website or web app: a calendar, a menu board, a status page, a photo frame
Choose your Home Assistant. If it isn\'t listed, type its address, for example http://192.168.1.50:8123.\n\nThe TV must be on the same network.
Didn\'t find Home Assistant by itself. Type its address instead.
That isn\'t a web address. It should look like http://192.168.1.50:8123.
%1$s answered, but it doesn\'t look like Home Assistant. Check the address and port (usually 8123).
Can\'t reach %1$s (%2$s). Check the address, and that Home Assistant is running and on the same network as the TV.
Choose the dashboard this TV shows. You can add more pages to rotate through later, in Settings.
Type the address of the page this TV shows. The TV\'s keyboard may have a microphone button, and the Google TV app on your phone can type for you.
The name Home Assistant shows for this TV
Leave empty to keep the current value. Type - to clear it.
Saves settings, without secrets, to a file you can copy with adb
Reads settings.json back from the same place
The dashboard list needs this TV to be signed in to Home Assistant. Open Sign-in and sign in once on this TV, or type the start page\'s address.
Home Assistant didn\'t list any dashboards this TV user can see.
This TV needs to be signed in to Home Assistant to list your dashboards.
The app stopped unexpectedly and reopened itself. Details are in Settings, under Status and about.
What the app did lately, with tokens blanked out
Save diagnostics for a bug report
State, settings without secrets, the last crash and the log, in one file

Saved to %1$s

Copy it to a computer with:
adb pull %1$s

It contains no passwords or tokens.
